stem:
On a breezy afternoon, Rekha fixes a paper firki on a stick on her terrace in Jaipur. After a few minutes, the firki starts spinning rapidly.

What makes the firki spin?

options.text: air that stays still around the firki
sunlight falling on the paper blades
moving air pushing against the blades
the bright colour of the paper

teacher.key_rationale: A firki spins only when moving air (wind) pushes against its shaped blades. Still air (A) does no turning, sunlight (B) and colour (D) are irrelevant surface features. Key recalculated as C.
